# Scroll Down MLB — fixture + snapshot corpus

This directory holds the parity baseline for the Phase 3 backend port of the
Scroll Down MLB deck builder.

## Provenance

- `games/` — 25 files (1 manifest + 23 captured game payloads + 1 synthetic).
  The captured payloads are verbatim copies of
  `scroll-down-web/web/tests/fixtures/games/` — real upstream game detail
  payloads from the live BFF at the time the migration began.
- `games/999125.json` — synthetic. Derived from `190125.json` by truncating
  the play list at index `50044`, marking the game live, and resetting
  the running score to that point. Exists solely to exercise the open-
  container path of `_group_into_containers` (live game, non-zero outs in
  the trailing half-inning, no inning-end signal). Not a parity fixture —
  intentionally has no matching snapshot, so the TS-parity harness skips
  it. Covered exclusively by `test_scroll_down_mlb_fixture_scenarios.py`.
- `snapshots/` — 23 files. Output of the current TypeScript builder
  (`buildCatchupCards`) when run against each captured fixture. Generated by
  `scroll-down-web/web/tests/unit/qa/_export-snapshots.test.ts`.

## Refresh procedure

When `buildCatchupCards` changes shape on the frontend side:

```bash
cd ~/Desktop/scroll-down-web/web
npx vitest run tests/unit/qa/_export-snapshots.test.ts
cp tests/fixtures/snapshots/*.json \
   ~/Desktop/sports-data-admin/api/tests/fixtures/scroll_down_mlb/snapshots/
```

## Backend parity expectations

The Python port intentionally diverges from the TS snapshots in two ways:

1. **`scoreAfter` is absent** from PlayPayload in the backend DTO. The
   spoiler-safety contract (Phase 2) forbids it. Parity tests strip
   `scoreAfter` from the TS snapshot before comparing.
2. **camelCase keys**: backend serializes the same logical fields under
   the same names; no transformation needed.

All other fields (selection, ordering, leverage tier, rhythm placement,
runner movements, labels, narrative) should match. Where they don't, the
parity test logs the deviation and the deliverable documents whether the
deviation is intentional or a port bug.
